title: Guide - Peace in the Psalms - Be still and know

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Peace in the Psalms. <short pause> This reading is called Be Still and Know. <short pause> We'll listen to the whole of Psalm forty-six. <short pause> It is a loud psalm in places... <short pause> and it has a great stillness near its end.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Find somewhere your body can be supported. <short pause> Feel what is steady beneath you. <short pause> You may have come here with a great deal of noise... from the news, from your home, from inside your own head. <short pause> Bring the noise along. <short pause> This psalm knows what to do with it.

As you listen, you will hear the word Selah. <short pause> No one is certain what it means, but many understand it as a place to pause. <short pause> So when you hear it, you don't need to do anything. <short pause> Let it be permission to stop for a breath.

God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. <short pause> Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea; <short pause> Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.

There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. <short pause> God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early. <short pause> The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved: he uttered his voice, the earth melted. <short pause> The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.

Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth. <short pause> He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire. <short pause> Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth. <short pause> The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Mountains falling. Waters roaring. Kingdoms moved. <short pause> The psalm doesn't ask us to pretend the world is calm. <short pause> It looks straight at everything that shakes... <short pause> and then it tells us what does not.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: In the middle of all that thundering water, there is another kind of water. <short pause> A river, with streams that make a city glad. <short pause> It doesn't roar. <short pause> It simply keeps arriving. <short pause> God's help can be like that... quieter than the trouble, and still flowing when the storm has tired itself out.

She shall not be moved, the psalm says of that city. <short pause> And the reason is not the strength of her walls. <short pause> God is in the midst of her. <short pause> You don't have to be unshakable. <short pause> You have Someone in the midst of you who is.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: And then, be still. <short pause> The old word behind it can mean let go... let your hands drop. <short pause> So let them drop now. <short pause> Be still, and know that I am God. <short pause> Be still, and know. <short pause> Be still. <short pause> Be.

What have your hands been gripping, as if the earth might give way without you? <short pause> Could you let it rest in His, for the length of one breath? <short pause> Breathe in... <short pause> God is our refuge. <short pause> Breathe out... <short pause> I can let go.

Let's pray. <short pause> God, our refuge and strength, <short pause> so much is shaking, and I cannot steady it all. <short pause> Be in the midst of me. <short pause> Be in the midst of the people and places I am afraid for. <short pause> Help me to let go, and to know that You are God. <short pause> Amen.

When the waters get loud again, remember the river. <short pause> And remember how the psalm ends... <short pause> the Lord of hosts is with us. <short pause> Let that be your place to pause. <short pause> Go in peace.
